Barbarian|PHB: Loyalty to my people filled me with strength in combat and made me dangerous.
My ancestors' spirits asked me to take on a mighty duty.
One day my fury took over in a fight, and something else seemed to steer my body into slaying every enemy within reach.
I set out to find myself spiritually and came back with an animal spirit that watches over and guides me.
A bolt of lightning hit me and I survived, then discovered a fresh power that let me exceed my old limits.
I had to pour my rage into combat, or else I might have turned into a killer who spared nobody.
Bard|PHB: Through plenty of mistakes and experiments, I woke up my hidden talent for bardic art.
My talent on stage drew in a master bard, and I was trained in the traditional ways.
I joined an informal society of thinkers and speakers to pick up fresh performance techniques and magic.
I felt driven to tell of the feats of great champions and make them live again through songs and tales.
I enrolled at a famed college to study ancient lore, magical secrets, and the craft of performing.
I picked up an instrument by chance and found at once that I knew how to play it.
Cleric|PHB: A being from beyond, working for the gods, summoned me to act as their agent on the mortal plane.
Seeing cruelty and suffering around me, I felt driven to stand against them.
My deity sent a sign I could not mistake, and I left everything behind to serve.
I was always pious, yet only after finishing a pilgrimage did I understand what I was meant to do.
I once worked in my faith's administration, but I needed to go out and carry its word into the world's bleakest corners.
My deity acts through me, so I follow commands, yet I have no idea what made me worthy.
Druid|PHB: I watched too many wild places laid waste and too much natural beauty spoiled by despoilers, so I joined a druid circle to resist nature's foes.
After running from a disaster, I found a home among a band of druids.
Animals always felt close to me, so I explored that gift to find its best use.
A druid became my friend, and the druidic teachings moved me enough to follow that guidance and repay the world.
Growing up, I noticed spirits everywhere that nobody else could see, so I sought druids who could explain my visions and teach me to talk to these beings.
Unnatural creatures have always repulsed me, so I plunged into druidic lore and became a defender of nature's balance.
Fighter|PHB: I longed to sharpen my fighting ability, so I enrolled in a war college.
I served as a knight's squire and learned combat, horse care, and honorable conduct, then chose that road for myself.
Dreadful monsters attacked my home and killed a person I loved, so I armed myself to destroy them and creatures like them.
Enlisting in the army taught me to fight alongside a unit.
Fighting filled my childhood, and I polished my skills guarding myself against anyone who wronged me.
Whatever weapon I held, I somehow knew how to wield it well.
Monk|PHB: I was picked to train at a remote monastery, where I learned the basic methods needed to someday master a discipline.
I wanted lessons that would deepen my grasp of existence and show me where I belong.
I fell through a gateway into the Shadowfell and sheltered in an odd monastery that taught me to resist the powers of darkness.
Grief crushed me after a loved one died, so I turned to philosophers for help with bearing the loss.
I sensed a unique force inside me and went looking for people able to help me bring it out and master it.
As a youth I was reckless and unruly until I saw my mistakes, then I joined a monastery to live with discipline.
Paladin|PHB: An astonishing being came to me and asked me to carry out a sacred mission.
An ancestor of mine never finished a sacred mission, so I mean to complete it.
The world is grim and cruel, so I chose to be a shining light against the spreading gloom.
I squired for a paladin and learned all I needed before swearing a sacred oath of my own.
Wickedness must be fought everywhere, and I feel bound to track it down and cleanse the world of it.
My steadfast faith led naturally to the paladin's path, and once I swore my vows I turned into my religion's holy sword.
Ranger|PHB: I found my calling sharpening my hunting by taking down dangerous beasts on the frontier of settled lands.
Animals have always trusted me, and a gentle word and touch could settle them.
A fierce urge to roam torments me, and the ranger life offered a purpose for constant travel.
I saw what happens once monsters leave the dark, so I made myself the first guard against the horrors beyond the borders of civilization.
A weathered old ranger showed me woodcraft and let me in on the hidden ways of untamed country.
Army service taught me my profession as I cleared trails and scouted enemy camps.
Rogue|PHB: Quick feet and a sharp wit came naturally to me, so I put them to work to get by.
A killer or burglar harmed me, so I trained to master that foe's methods and fight such enemies better.
A seasoned rogue spotted potential in me and passed on a handful of handy tricks.
I chose to build a career on my good fortune, though I know my skills still need work.
I fell in with a band of toughs who taught me to get my way by stealth instead of open conflict.
Glittering trinkets and bags of coin tempt me, provided I can grab them without risking my neck.
Sorcerer|PHB: At my birth, the water in our house froze, the milk soured, or the iron became copper, and my family thinks it signaled stranger things ahead.
A terrible shock to my body or feelings released my hidden magic, and I have struggled to master it since.
My family never mentioned my forebears and dodged my questions, until my odd talents appeared and the whole truth of my bloodline emerged.
A monster menaced a friend, fear flooded me, and I struck back by instinct with a blast of power from deep inside.
A stranger noticed something unusual in me and taught me to command my gift.
I got out of a magical blaze without a scratch, yet I knew I had changed, and strange abilities started showing that I am only starting to grasp.
Warlock|PHB: Wandering through a place no one should enter, I met an otherworldly being who offered me a pact.
I was reading an odd book from a deserted library when the being who would be my patron appeared right in front of me.
I fell into my patron's grasp when I walked through a magic gate by mistake.
In the depths of a crisis I begged any power that would hear me, and the thing that replied became my patron.
My patron to be came to me in dreams and promised great power in return for my service.
An ancestor of mine once struck a bargain with my patron, who was set on binding me to identical terms.
Wizard|PHB: An aged wizard picked me out of a group of hopefuls to be an apprentice.
Stranded in the woods, I was found by a hedge wizard who sheltered me and showed me magic from the ground up.
Stories of great wizards filled my childhood and I wanted their path, so I worked hard to get into a magic academy and did.
A wizard in my family decided I had enough brains to study the craft.
Exploring an ancient crypt, library, or shrine, I came upon a spellbook, and it drove me at once to study the wizard's craft.
I showed a gift for arcane arts as a child, and once old enough to leave, I went off to study more magic and grow stronger.

Acolyte|PHB: As a child I fled my home and took shelter in a temple.
My relatives handed me over to a temple because they could not or would not raise me.
I was raised in a home with deep religious belief, so serving one or more deities felt natural.
A passionate sermon reached deep into my soul and stirred me toward the service of the faith.
I trailed a loved one, a childhood companion, or someone I respected into religious life.
Meeting a genuine divine servant inspired me so much that I joined a religious order straight away.
Charlatan|PHB: Nobody watched over me, and my talent for steering people let me get by.
Early in life I saw how trusting people are and how simple they are to take advantage of.
I got into plenty of scrapes, but I always talked myself free.
I teamed up with a swindler who showed me the craft.
A fraud once cheated my family, so I studied the trade to avoid ever being tricked that way again.
Poverty, or the fear of it, pushed me to pick up the tricks that kept want away.
Criminal|PHB: In my younger years I resented authority and saw crime as my best weapon against oppression and tyranny.
I had no choice but to live this way, because it was my only means of staying alive.
I joined a crowd of rogues and scoundrels, and they taught me my specialty.
One of my parents or relatives passed on my specialty so I could join the family trade.
Leaving home, I landed a spot in a guild of thieves or another criminal outfit.
Boredom pushed me into crime as a pastime, and I found I had real talent for it.
Entertainer|PHB: My relatives earned a living by performing, so following in their steps made sense.
I understood people so well that my tales or ballads could draw out their laughter or tears.
I left home to chase after a troupe of wandering minstrels.
Watching one bard perform showed me right then what I was meant to be.
I made money performing at street corners and gradually earned a reputation.
A performer who traveled the roads adopted me and showed me the trade.
Folk Hero|PHB: My family taught me the difference between right and wrong.
Stories of heroes thrilled me, and I dreamed of becoming more than a common person.
My dull everyday life bored me, so when someone had to step forward and do right, I grabbed the chance.
A parent or other relative went adventuring, and that courage inspired me.
An old mad hermit prophesied at my birth that I would do great deeds.
I have always defended people weaker than myself.
Guild Artisan (Guild Merchant)|PHB: A master took me on as an apprentice and taught me how the guild worked.
I kept a secret for a guild artisan or finished a job for one, and was accepted as an apprentice in exchange.
A relative in the guild found me a spot.
I was always skilled with my fingers, so I seized the opening to pick up a trade.
I wanted out of my situation at home and a chance at a new life.
A mentor taught me the core skills of my craft, but finishing my training required joining the guild.
Hermit|PHB: Foes destroyed my good name, and I escaped into the wild to dodge more slander.
Being alone suits me well while I look for peace within.
I disliked the folks I called friends, so heading out solo came easily.
I felt driven to give up my past, though I did so very unwillingly, and at times I regret it.
I lost it all, including my home, family, and friends, so going alone was my only option.
The excess and decay of society sickened me, so I walked away from it.
Noble|PHB: My family is old and renowned, and protecting its good name fell to me.
My family fell into disgrace, and I plan to restore our honor.
My family only lately received its title, and the rise tossed us into a bewildering new world.
My family holds a title, but no ancestor has achieved anything notable since we received it.
My relatives are all extraordinary people, and I hope to measure up to them.
I want to expand the power and reach of my family.
Outlander|PHB: I spent much of my youth in the wild and grew to love living that way.
Even as a child, I could not stand the stench of cities and chose nature instead.
I discovered the evil hidden among untamed lands and swore to battle it.
My kin lived at the edge of civilized lands, and my family taught me the ways of staying alive.
Following a tragedy, I withdrew into the wilderness and left my former life behind.
My kin moved away from settled lands, and I grew used to the new surroundings.
Sage|PHB: Being naturally inquisitive, I gathered my belongings and set off for a university to study the world.
My mentor's lessons showed me new possibilities within my field of study.
I read voraciously as a child and taught myself a great deal about my favorite subject.
I came upon an ancient library and combed its texts, which left me craving still more knowledge.
A wizard was impressed by me and said I was wasting my talents, urging me to get an education and put my gifts to use.
A parent or relative gave me simple schooling that sparked my appetite, so I departed home to build upon it.
Sailor|PHB: Pirates kidnapped me into service on their vessel, and I labored there until I got away.
I yearned for far horizons, so I took a job as a deckhand on a merchant vessel.
A relative of mine worked as a sailor and brought me out to sea.
I had to flee my community fast, so I hid aboard a ship, and once the crew caught me, I worked to pay for the voyage.
Raiders hit my community, and I took refuge aboard a vessel until I could get revenge.
My hometown held few prospects for me, so I went off to seek my fortune elsewhere.
Soldier|PHB: I signed up with the militia to guard my community against monsters.
A kinsman of mine soldiered before me, so I chose to carry on that family custom.
The lord of my region made me join the army.
War tore through my homeland during my childhood, and combat was all I ever knew.
I craved glory and riches, so I signed up with a mercenary band and sold my blade to whoever paid best.
Invaders struck my homeland, and I felt duty-bound to arm myself and protect my people.
Urchin|PHB: A longing to travel made me leave my family and see the world, and I fend for myself.
I fled a rotten household and made a path for myself in the world.
Monsters destroyed my village, leaving me its only survivor, and I had to work out how to stay alive.
A well-known thief took care of several orphans including me, and we earned our keep through spying and theft.
I came to on the streets one day, hungry and alone, remembering nothing from when I was small.
My parents passed away and nobody was left to care for me, so I brought myself up.
